metadata.title: Spicy Pepper Soup Recipe (Milagu Rasam)
metadata.description:
Spicy Pepper Soup is very popular in South India. It tastes great with hot steamed rice and a tsp of ghee. It is prepared with cumin seeds, pepper and garlic. It is also very comforting and effective when taken during fever or cold.

summary.brief: A woman prepares, cooks, and serves a spicy pepper soup.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a title card and then shows the host displaying bowls of chopped tomatoes, garlic, peppercorns, cumin, tamarind, and other spices. She uses a mortar and pestle to crush peppercorns, garlic and cumin together, then tempers mustard seeds (and a few fenugreek seeds) in hot oil in a pot. She adds the crushed mixture along with coriander powder, a pinch of turmeric, and a little chili powder, stirring briefly. Next she pours in the chopped tomatoes, a pinch of salt and tamarind puree, adds water, and lets the mixture boil for several minutes. After simmering she adds a pinch of asafoetida and fresh coriander leaves, checks the seasoning, then strains the hot rasam into a serving bowl. Finally she garnishes the soup with chopped cilantro (coriander) and presents the finished bowl before the video ends with a closing title screen.

action.detailed: Crush peppercorns, garlic and cumin together, temper mustard seeds in oil, add the crushed mixture with coriander powder, turmeric and chili powder, then add chopped tomatoes, salt, tamarind puree and water, bring to a boil, simmer, stir, strain into a serving bowl and garnish with cilantro.

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
Spicy Pepper Soup is very popular in South India. It tastes great with hot steamed rice and a tsp of ghee. It is prepared with cumin seeds, pepper and garlic. It is also very comforting and effective when taken during fever or cold.

#souprecipe #peppersoup
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a title card and then shows the host displaying bowls of chopped tomatoes, garlic, peppercorns, cumin, tamarind, and other spices. She uses a mortar and pestle to crush peppercorns, garlic and cumin together, then tempers mustard seeds (and a few fenugreek seeds) in hot oil in a pot. She adds the crushed mixture along with coriander powder, a pinch of turmeric, and a little chili powder, stirring briefly. Next she pours in the chopped tomatoes, a pinch of salt and tamarind puree, adds water, and lets the mixture boil for several minutes. After simmering she adds a pinch of asafoetida and fresh coriander leaves, checks the seasoning, then strains the hot rasam into a serving bowl. Finally she garnishes the soup with chopped cilantro (coriander) and presents the finished bowl before the video ends with a closing title screen.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
